A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison, including material reorganized between the main text and appendices.

before.justification: V1 reports original simulated-feedback experiments on Assistant, Summary and Summary+, including estimation errors, mis-prediction rates, sensitivity analyses and personalized response examples.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds response win rates, evaluations across diverse user profiles and experiments with another response-generation backbone.

M1.justification: AMPLe names the existing vol-mo method. The modified Bayesian update, MAP estimation, volume-based query selection and Metropolis–Hastings sampling remain. The rewritten acquisition score preserves query rankings; the uniform sampling proposal was already described in v1.

E1.justification: The three datasets and language-generation tasks remain unchanged. V2 expands the represented simulated-user population beyond the selected profiles to groups across profile space in Assistant and Summary (Section 5.3.1 and Appendix C.3).

E2.justification: The evaluated preference-learning comparators remain rnd-un, vol-un and rnd-mo against vol-mo. Rame et al. supplies an additional query-generation backbone for all four methods in Figures 16–17. Newly discussed related works are not added as experimental baselines.

E3.justification: V2 adds response win-rate evaluation using round-10 estimates and rejection-sampled generations, profile-region error aggregation at rounds 10, 30 and 50, and evaluations with Rame-based query pools. These substantially extend the evaluation design. The existing RiC pool construction and static/dynamic-context procedures remain.

E4.justification: New analyses test dependence on the true user profile and on the response-generation backbone (Section 5.3.1, Appendices C.3–C.4, Figures 14–17). These broaden robustness evidence beyond v1's noise, dimensionality and parameter-sensitivity studies, which are retained.

E5.justification: V2 newly states that evaluation metrics use means and standard errors across five seeds. It removes the three-seed mean description from the otherwise retained qualitative tables. The ten-seed feedback-noise analysis remains. These reporting changes do not establish that existing experiments were rerun with more seeds.

E6.justification: V2 Table 1 newly reports vol-mo win rates of 75.70% against rnd-mo, 83.91% against vol-un and 82.35% against rnd-un. Diverse-profile and alternative-backbone error results are also added. Existing mis-prediction values are unchanged from v1 Table 1 to v2 Table 4.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 revises the counterexample from v1's growing-pool argument to a sufficiently large fixed pool with increasing feedback rounds, removes reward-vector scaling and specifies convergence in probability. V2 also explicitly asserts that the error bound tends to zero; conditions omitted from the informal theorem remain in Appendix A.2.

C1.justification: Both versions claim feedback-efficient estimation of implicit, multi-dimensional preferences through modified Bayesian updates and active queries, supported by theory and language-generation experiments. Naming the framework AMPLe and adding supporting evaluations do not substantially change these core contributions.

C2.justification: V2 acknowledges worse performance under dynamic contexts, replacing v1's statement that varying contexts do not affect estimation. It also discusses generation reward variance and interprets the new experiments as supporting applicability across backbones. The static-preference and unresolved convergence-rate limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 adds a repository link claiming public code and specifies 50,000 burn-in iterations and lag 10 for sampling. However, v1's per-task default beta/gamma settings and explicit deterministic mis-prediction-scoring description are omitted. Dataset links, reward-model links and query-pool construction details remain.

R1.justification: V2 adds Li et al. (2023) and Poddar et al. (2024), including discussion of Poddar's fixed comparison collection, while removing several general alignment-variant references. It more explicitly relates vol-un and rnd-un to Sadigh and Hwang, respectively, without substantially changing the overall research position.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method explanation and conclusion are extensively rewritten. V2 introduces AMPLe terminology, subdivides the problem formulation, reorganizes results and ablations, and restructures the appendices into theory, experimental details, additional experiments and qualitative examples.

P2.justification: V2 adds overview and posterior-update illustrations, a win-rate matrix, profile heatmaps and backbone-comparison plots. It relocates the original mis-prediction table and personalization traces to Appendix C, changes sensitivity-plot colors and line styles, and reformats the qualitative tables and captions.

improvement.justification: The broader simulated-user and backbone tests address v1's reliance on selected profiles and one generation backbone, while clearer explanations and statistical reporting improve assessability. The gain is limited by incomplete documentation of the new win-rate evaluation and removal of some earlier parameter details. Overall, v2 provides stronger empirical support and clearer presentation, with remaining reproducibility gaps.
